Synopsis:
    Global equity funds saw $15.52B in net outflows for the week ending Sept 9, the largest since March 18, driven by a $32.27B exodus from US equities. The trigger: a US-Iran war-driven oil price surge pushing Brent to $109.97/bbl, stoking inflation fears. US PPI data confirmed inflation remained firm in August. Bond flows were muted, money markets attracted $10.72B, and emerging markets ended an eight-week buying streak. Markets are clearly repositioning ahead of an anticipated Fed rate hike.
